# Confidence Intervals

If you did many experiments, x % of the confidence interval should catch the true value in their range.


## Tutorial 1

```{r}
n <- 200
mean <- 0.824
sd <- 0.042
# Standard Error
se <- sd /sqrt(n)
conf_levels <- c(0.90, 0.95, 0.98, 0.99)

# (100% area - x% you want to ensure) / 2(left and right)

for (cl in conf_levels){
    alpha <- 1 - cl
    z <- qnorm(1- alpha/2)
    range_error <- z * se
    lower <- mean - range_error
    upper <- mean + range_error
    cat(sprintf("Critical Value: %.3f, Confidence Interval: [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n", z, lower, upper))
}
```

## Exercise 6

```{r}
sigma <- 0.05
E <- 0.01
conf_levels <- c(0.95, 0.99)
for (cl in conf_levels){
    alpha <- 1 - cl
    z <- qnorm(1- alpha/2)
    range_error <- z * se
    lower <- mean - range_error
    upper <- mean + range_error
    cat(sprintf("Critical Value: %.3f, Confidence Interval: [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n", z, lower, upper))
    
    n <- 1
    current_error <- Inf
    while (current_error > E) {
        n <- n + 1
        # CLT: the average of variance should decrease with sqrt(n)^{-1}
        current_error <- z * (sigma / sqrt(n))
    }
    cat(sprintf("Necessary Sample Size n = %d\n\n", n))

}
```

## Exercise 7

```{r}
#  The size is population is known
N <- 200
n<- 50
mean <- 75
sd <- 10
se <- (sd / sqrt(n)) * sqrt((N - n) / (N - 1))
conf_levels <- c(0.95)

for (cl in conf_levels){
    alpha <- 1 - cl
    z <- qnorm(1- alpha/2)
    range_error <- z * se
    lower <- mean - range_error
    upper <- mean + range_error
    cat(sprintf("Critical Value: %.3f, Confidence Interval: [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n", z, lower, upper))
    prob <- pnorm(75, mean = mean, sd = se) - pnorm(73, mean = mean, sd = se)
    cat(sprintf("The degree of confidence %% that the mean of all 200 grades is 74 ± 1 : %.1f%%\n", prob * 100))
}
```

## Tutorial 2

```{r}
n <- 10
mean_x <- 4.38
sd_x <- 0.06
se <- sd_x / sqrt(n)
conf_levels <- c(0.95, 0.99)
for (cl in conf_levels) {
  alpha <- 1 - cl
  
  # --- Z ---
  z_val <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
  error_z <- z_val * se
  ci_z <- c(mean_x - error_z, mean + error_z)
  
  # --- t-distribution ---
  # df(Degree of freedom) = n - 1 
  # qt: quantile
  t_val <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = n - 1)
  error_t <- t_val * se
  ci_t <- c(mean_x - error_t, mean + error_t)
  
  cat(sprintf("【Confidence Interval %.0f%%】\n", cl * 100))
  cat(sprintf("  Large Sample (Z: %.3f): [%.4f, %.4f]\n", z_val, ci_z[1], ci_z[2]))
  cat(sprintf("  Small Sample (t: %.3f): [%.4f, %.4f]\n", t_val, ci_t[1], ci_t[2]))
}

```

### Student
* William Gossett, an employee of the Irish beer company Guinness, published the book under the pseudonym "Student" to conceal his identity.


## Exercise 8

```{r}
n <- 40
x <- 24
p_hat <- x / n
sd_x <- sqrt( p_hat * (1 - p_hat))

conf_levels <- c(0.95)
for (cl in conf_levels) {
    alpha <- 1 - cl
    z <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
    se <-  sd_x / sqrt(n)

    # Confidence Interval
    lower <- p_hat - z * se
    upper <- p_hat + z * se
    cat(sprintf("Critical Value: %.3f, Confidence Interval: [%.4f, %.4f]\n\n", z, lower, upper))
}  

```
